text: emma: Heads-up: I just triaged an automated report from our fuzzing infra — DOM XSS in the /login widget. Low user interaction but reproducible. Attaching quick repro and suggestion. luke: ugh. where in the widget? emma: the `next` redirect query param is inserted into the page with `innerHTML` in login.js. repro: `https://app.redwood.test/login?next=%3Cimg%20src%3Dx%20onerror%3Dalert(1)%3E` triggers. emma: snippet:```js // login.js (simplified) const next = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('next') || '/dashboard'; document.querySelector('#return-link').innerHTML = `Continue`; ``` luke: oh yeah that's classic DOM XSS. Not sanitizing or encoding. rachel: what envs are affected? prod? staging? emma: verified on staging and a quick check shows same code path in frontend main bundle v2.8.1 deployed to production. I did not trigger a stored payload. Seems reflected/DOM only. javi: severity? do we need a user notice? emma: marking as P2. Exploit requires user visiting crafted link; user interaction. No evidence of token exfil yet. Recommend immediate mitigation + fix. luke: mitigation plan: 1) quick WAF rule to block `next` containing `<` or `onerror` 2) add CSP directive as belt-and-suspenders 3) proper fix in code to textContent/encode or whitelist redirect targets. emma: agree. also add audit log event for any future changes to redirect param handling (SEC-LOG). nina: I can validate the WAF rule on staging and run regression tests. rachel: I'll stand up canary with WAF rule in front of prod web via the edge rule set. deploy-bot will show status. deploy-bot: deploy triggered: edge-rules/waf-temp-block-next-payload -> staging (id: dr-9821) nina: confirmed staging blocked the payload, 403 with rule 1007. No breakage in normal logins in 15m smoke. luke: I'll open a PR with proper fix: replace `innerHTML` with safe link creation + redirect whitelist. PR: https://git.redwood.internal/frontend/pulls/4567 (WIP). emma: please include a unit test that rejects non-whitelisted hosts and an E2E that checks no script executes when `next` contains tags. javi: timeline? can we ship fix today to prod behind a feature flag? luke: yes, aiming for cherry-pick to v2.8.x and deploy to prod today if tests pass. cicd-bot: pipeline started: frontend/4567 -> ci-frontend-7 -> tests running rachel: also, can we rotate any session cookies or tokens? If there was no evidence of token capture, rotating may be overkill and risky. Thoughts? emma: I agree we don't have indicators. Instead: query access logs for suspicious `next` hits with script-like payloads over last 48h. Add temporary telemetry to log full query param for future triage (retention 7d). Add audit log entry for the fix and WAF change. nina: running log query now, will post results. nina: log query result: 6 hits with suspicious payloads in last 48h from distinct IPs; all were non-authenticated probes and stopped by staging. No auth cookie present. emma: good — no evidence of session theft. escalate to SOC? low priority but please note in morning triage. javi: I'll create SEC ticket SEC-3214 capturing vuln, mitigation, timeline, and comms. Assign to luke for fix, nina for verification, rachel for rollout. luke: PR green tests, ready for review. https://git.redwood.internal/frontend/pulls/4567 emma: code review notes: ensure redirect whitelist is config-driven and gated by RBAC so only infra team can edit. Also add audit log event when whitelist entries change (we'll record actor, timestamp, old/new). javi: good call — link to audit plan: https://confluence.redwood.internal/security/audit-guidelines (internal). luke: making whitelist behind admin setting + server-side validation. Will add audit emit to admin api. cicd-bot: deploy succeeded: frontend v2.8.2 -> prod (canary 10% -> 100%). rachel: 10% canary looks clean. WAF rule still active for extra safety during rollout. nina: ran E2E and manual probes on prod canary — no execution. emma: I've updated the incident notes and included POC and mitigation steps. Added follow-ups: - SEC-3214: post-mortem due in 3 business days - Add unit + e2e coverage for redirect param handling (luke) - Implement audit events for redirect whitelist changes (luke + infra) - Add CSP report-only for 7 days to monitor (rachel) - Verify KMS/audit integration for admin change events (emma) javi: do we need customer comms? emma: not necessary. No data exfiltration or active exploit. We'll note internally and include fix in next security bulletin. luke: PR merged. closing WAF rule after 24h of clean prod telemetry. emma: thanks everyone. great coordinated response. I'll attach the post-mortem draft once SEC-3214 is created. :thumbsup:
